hindi: ऐसा हो सकता है कि सूर्य शनि को नहीं मार रहा लेकिन शनि सूर्य को मार रहा है तो ऐसे में क्या होगा बहुत अच्छा बाप है बेटा उसको मारेगा जबान से नहीं हो सकता है हाथों से भी मारे
says: It can be one-sided: the Sun is not hitting Saturn but Saturn is hitting the Sun. Then even a very good father gets hit by the son, in words and possibly with hands too.
cells_derived_method: Which side hits depends on aspect direction (Saturn's aspect falls on the Sun but not the other way); the house and sign of the Sun decide whether it is the father or the son house that suffers.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Sun in own sign on the 9th (father's house), Saturn from Aquarius on the 3rd house hits it with the 7th aspect, so a good father is hurt by his child; lagna Sagittarius.
Derived: Sun in own sign on the 5th (children house), Saturn in Aquarius on the 11th hits it with the 7th aspect, so a child's harsh behaviour shows up; lagna Aries.

ambiguity: Whether the chart in question is the father's or the son's is not stated; he speaks of the parent complaining, so the parent's chart is assumed.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Saturn aspecting the Sun is a classic sign of strained father-son ties; the one-sided reading is his own.

hindi: तो लोग कहते हैं य बच्चा हमें पीटता है मारता है गाली बगता है आपकी कुंडली में दोष है अब आप उसके लिए कुछ भी बड़े से बड़ा उपाय कर लो व नहीं सुधरेगा
says: Parents complain that their child beats and abuses them; he says the fault is in their chart, and no remedy, however big, will make that child reform. This is his claim for the Saturn-hitting-Sun case.
cells_derived_method: none: a statement that remedies will not reform the child; not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'आपकी कुंडली में दोष है' is addressed to the parent; the condition is the Saturn-on-Sun pattern from the previous row.
classical_check: Differs: classical texts offer pacification of Sun and Saturn and do not call such a fault unfixable.

hindi: उसके लिए आपको उससे कटिंग करनी पड़ेगी रिश्ते की कॉर्ड कट करना ही पड़ेगा
says: For such a child the only way is to cut yourself off from him: the cord of the relationship has to be cut. This is his practical remedy, a tradition claim recorded as spoken and not as family advice.
cells_derived_method: none: a remedy statement that is not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'कटिंग' is read as cutting emotional and relational ties, not necessarily a legal or physical break.
classical_check: Silent: classical Jyotish remedies are worship, mantra, charity and gems, not cutting a relationship.

hindi: और 36 किस्म के उपाय करने पड़े होंगे आप कहोगे मैं अपने जीवन के अंदर कोई स्टोन नहीं पहनना चाहता
says: Beyond cutting the cord there would be 36 kinds of remedies to do. He then voices the likely objection from the listener: I do not want to wear any stone in my life.
cells_derived_method: none: a general remark on the scale of remedies; not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: '36 किस्म' may be a figure of speech for many remedies; 'होंगे' leaves it open whether it is a requirement or a hypothetical.
classical_check: Silent: no classical text counts 36 remedies for this problem.

hindi: स्टोन सबसे पावरफुल उपाय है क्योंकि वो फिल्टर है
says: A gemstone is the most powerful of all remedies, he says, because it works as a filter for the planet's rays.
cells_derived_method: none: a general ranking claim about remedies; the stone to wear depends on the planet and is not named here.
ambiguity: 'पावरफुल' is not tested against mantra or charity in this sentence.
classical_check: Partly agrees: ratna dharana is a classical remedy and widely used, but classical texts do not rank it above mantra or daana.

hindi: वो स्टोन आपके ग्रहों की रेज और आपकी बॉडी के बीच में प्रिज्म ट कर देता है और उतनी ही फिल्टर होती है रेज जितनी जानी चाहिए बैलेंसिंग करता है
says: The mechanism he gives: the stone sits like a prism between the planet's rays and your body, letting through only as much of the ray as should pass, and in this way it balances the planet's influence.
cells_derived_method: none: a general mechanism claim, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'प्रिज्म ट कर देता है' is a garbled phrase; read as 'puts a prism'.
classical_check: Silent: the prism and ray-filter explanation is a modern gloss, not classical.

hindi: अब आप कहते हम नीलम नहीं पहन सकते कौन इतने लाख फूके तो कोई चिंता नहीं है
says: If you say you cannot wear a blue sapphire (neelam, Saturn's stone), then the alternative would be chanting mantra in lakhs, and he asks who will do that many lakhs; so the stone is the practical choice. The last clause says there is no worry, spoken half in irony.
cells_derived_method: none: the stone-versus-mantra comparison is not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'फूके' (blow or chant) is read as mantra repetition in lakhs; 'कोई चिंता नहीं है' could mean 'then no problem' or be ironic. Neelam as a stone for Saturn is a standard link but is not stated here as a rule.
classical_check: Agrees: neelam is the gemstone of Saturn and japa of Saturn mantras is the classical alternative; the required number of repetitions is in the tens of thousands, not lakhs.

gist: Aside to a listener named Mona: she had saved 10 minutes because she had already given 50 earlier, so time was left over; unclear what the figures refer to.

hindi: अगर आप स्टोन नहीं पहनना चाहते तो उतने साल तक वह कष्ट चलेगा या धन की बलि दे दो
says: If you refuse to wear a stone, the trouble will keep going for as many years as it was due to last, or else you give a sacrifice of money instead. So there are two choices: the stone or paying with money.
cells_derived_method: none: the trade-off between stone and money is not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'उतने साल' refers to the length of the affliction, which could be a dasha or a transit period; it is not named here.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not describe money as a bali in place of a gemstone.

hindi: धन की बलि नहीं देनी तो उतने सालों साल के लिए तैयार रहो आप दुखी रहोगे उतने साल जो कि पूरी जिंदगी का नासूर भी बन सकता है
says: If you will not give up money either, then be ready to remain unhappy for that many years, and the unhappiness can turn into a lifelong sore. It is a warning that refusing both remedies prolongs the suffering.
cells_derived_method: none: a warning about unremedied suffering, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'नासूर' (a chronic wound) is a metaphor for a permanent hurt.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not warn in this way.

hindi: इसलिए पैसे तो फूकने पड़ेंगे अब कहेंगे लोग पैसे ही नहीं तो क्या करें
says: So money has to be spent, he says, because remedies cost. Then he voices the common reply from people, that they have no money and ask what to do.
cells_derived_method: none: a general statement about the cost of remedies, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'फूकने' means burn or spend; here he means spending money on remedies.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts value daana and ritual spending but do not set this as a general rule.

hindi: शिक्षा लो पैसे कैसे आएंगे उसके उपाय करो पैसे फ्री फंड में नहीं
says: His answer to having no money: take his teaching, learn how money will come, and do the remedies for it; money does not arrive free of cost. The sentence stops at the end of this slice and is probably completed in the next.
cells_derived_method: none: general advice on earning the money for remedies, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'शिक्षा लो' could mean get an education or take instruction; the sentence is cut off at the slice end, so the rest is unknown.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not discuss how to fund remedies.

hindi: आएंगे पैसे लक्ष्मी है पैसे बुद्ध है
says: Completing the last sentence of the previous slice (money does not come free of cost), he says money is Lakshmi and money is 'buddh'. The second word is unclear: it could be wisdom (buddhi) or Mercury (Budh) as the trade planet.
cells_derived_method: none: a general statement about money, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'बुद्ध' may be a cut-off 'बुद्धि' (intelligence) or 'बुध' (Mercury); no planet is named, so none is recorded. 'आएंगे' belongs to the previous slice's sentence.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Lakshmi is the goddess of wealth; classically wealth is read from Jupiter, Venus, Mercury and the 2nd and 11th houses.

hindi: पैसे कृपा से आते हैं कृपा लेना सीखो
says: Money comes through grace (kripa) and not by effort alone, so you should learn how to receive grace. He moves the cause of money from effort to being worthy of grace.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: He does not say here whose grace; the next slice names Varuna and Krishna.
classical_check: Silent: classical wealth rules use houses, lords and yogas; grace as the source is devotional framing.

hindi: आपको कोई ना कोई गुरु मिल जाएगा जो रास्ता दिखा देगा यह गांठ बांध के चलो और जो छोड़ दिया वो छोड़ दिया
says: Some guru will turn up who shows you the way; tie this in a knot (keep it firmly in mind) and walk on, and what has been let go is let go. He promises guidance to a seeker and tells him not to look back.
cells_derived_method: none: a general encouragement, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'जो छोड़ दिया वो छोड़ दिया' may mean forgetting what was given up as bali or dropping the past in general.
classical_check: Silent as a rule; a guru is classically read from the 9th house and Jupiter.

hindi: धन पर बलि दो तन मन धन नाम से क्लास है
says: Give the sacrifice on wealth. He sorts sacrifice (bali) into three classes called tan (body), man (mind) and dhan (money).
cells_derived_method: none: a classification of sacrifice types, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'क्लास' means kind or category; 'धन पर बलि दो' opens the money bali which is explained in the next sentence.
classical_check: Silent: the tan-man-dhan class scheme is his own; the classical equivalent is daana, tapas and seva.

hindi: या तन की बलि दो या मन की दो या धन की बलि दो धन की बली सर्वश्रेष्ठ है वो फिर कमा सकते हैं
says: You may pay with body, with mind or with money, but the money sacrifice is the best because you can earn money again. He picks money as the cheapest thing to lose.
cells_derived_method: none: a ranking of the three sacrifices, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: He does not say how much money is to be given.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical remedies rank daana (giving) highly; the ranking over body and mind sacrifice is his own.

gist: Broken caption 'लेकिन आपके बस की नहीं हो रही तो आपका वाला बदलो वाला बदलेगा कोई दूसरा वो वाला बदलो ग सेट होगा': possibly an advice to change one's kind of sacrifice if money is not possible, but not decodable.

hindi: मानो आपके गृह आसानी से उने नहीं देंगे कृपा मांगो कृष्ण को साथ लेकर चलो बहुत सी चीजें इसके अंदर
says: Suppose your planets will not easily let go of you (the clause is garbled); then ask for grace and walk with Krishna by your side, since many things are included in that.
cells_derived_method: none: a general devotional remedy, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: 'आपके गृह' is read as 'आपके ग्रह' (your planets); 'उने नहीं देंगे' is broken, so the object of 'will not give' is unknown.
classical_check: Agrees broadly: worship of Krishna is a classical Jupiter and Mercury remedy; the exact claim here is unclear.

hindi: शनि आपका यहां बैठ गया अब शनि यह घी है यह तेल है यह यहां जाकर के उच्च का होता है
says: With Saturn placed here, ghee and oil meet (Venus-type ghee and Saturn's oil), and on reaching this place Saturn becomes exalted. He points at a sign on his figure and says Saturn is exalted there.
cells_derived_method: The sign is Libra; the house it falls in decides which life area gets Saturn's strong result: the 4th house gives a steady home and property, the 11th gains and elder-sibling support.

Derived: exalted Saturn on the 11th gives lasting gains and a steady network; lagna Sagittarius.

ambiguity: 'यहां' points at a sign on the board and is not named in the caption; Libra is inferred from the next sentences (Varuna's house, with exaltation).
classical_check: Agrees: Saturn is exalted in Libra, the sign of Venus.

hindi: शनि है जाम लगा हुआ है बहुत तगड़ा कहीं व जा नहीं सकते
says: Here Saturn is in a jam: he is locked in very strongly and can go nowhere. In that sign Saturn is stuck and firm, not moving on.
cells_derived_method: The house shows what is held fixed: the 6th holds disputes and debts in place, the 12th holds confinement or distant residence.

Derived: Saturn jammed in Libra on the 12th, expenses and confinement are held fixed, with a stay that is hard to leave; lagna Scorpio.

hindi: समुद्र है वरुण देव वरुण के घर में शनि उच्च का होता है
says: The sea is the god Varuna, and in Varuna's house Saturn is exalted. He ties Saturn's exaltation to the sea-god's own sign.

Derived: exalted Saturn on the 7th gives a steady, mature, possibly older spouse and durable partnerships; lagna Aries.
Derived: exalted Saturn on the 10th gives a strong, lasting career and authority; lagna Capricorn.

ambiguity: He does not say which sign is Varuna's house; Libra is read from the classical exaltation and his scheme in which Neptune shares Libra with Venus.
classical_check: Agrees on the result: Saturn is exalted in Libra; the Varuna-house explanation is his own.

hindi: समुद्र किसी को जाने आने नहीं देता समुद्र के कोई कंट्रोल नहीं कर सकता

cells_derived_method: none: a description of Varuna's nature, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: It is an explanation attached to the exaltation claim and carries no sign by itself.
classical_check: Silent: Neptune and Varuna's control are not part of classical Jyotish.

hindi: समुद्र के ऊपर सवारी सवारी करना मजाक नहीं है उसके एक हिस्से पर आप नाव लेकर जा सकते हैं समुद्र की सवारी नहीं हो सकती
says: Riding the sea is no joke: you can take a boat over a small part of it, but you cannot master the sea. Varuna's vastness lets people cross, never command.
cells_derived_method: none: a description of Varuna's nature, not house or sign dependent.
ambiguity: A metaphor used for the same point as the previous sentence.
classical_check: Silent: Neptune is not classical.

hindi: शनि का य आनंद है शनि कहता बस छा गया मैं
says: This is Saturn's delight: in Varuna's sea Saturn says, enough, I have taken over everything. Saturn feels fully at home and dominant in the sea-god's sign.
cells_derived_method: none: a descriptive remark about the exalted state; the house-wise results are in the other rows on this sign.
ambiguity: The sentence starts at the end of one slice and finishes in the next; the sign (Libra) is carried from the previous sentences.
classical_check: Agrees: an exalted planet is at its strongest.

hindi: समुद्र में कितना कुछ गुप्त पड़ा है सारा तो लक्ष्मी समुद्र के अंदर य धरती के गर्भ में क्या क्या पड़ा कोई नहीं जानता
says: A great deal lies hidden in the sea; all the wealth (Lakshmi) is inside the sea or in the earth's womb, and nobody knows what is there. He ties hidden riches to the sea and underground, the realms of Varuna and Saturn.
cells_derived_method: none: a karaka statement, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: None; it extends his earlier line that wealth lies in the earth's womb.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Saturn is karaka of minerals, oil and what is underground; the sea link is his own.

hindi: इसलिए शनि सर्वोत्तम फल देता है यहां
says: Because of that hidden wealth, Saturn gives his best fruit in this place, in Varuna's sign. He grades Saturn in the sea-god's sign as the very best case.
cells_derived_method: The house sets what the best fruit is: 2nd for wealth and speech, 5th for intellect and children, 9th for fortune and dharma.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Saturn in Libra on the 2nd gives wealth built steadily and a measured manner of speech; lagna Virgo.
Derived: Saturn in Libra on the 5th gives deep thinking and well-timed children; lagna Gemini.
Derived: Saturn in Libra on the 9th gives fortune after effort and a disciplined sense of dharma; lagna Aquarius.

ambiguity: 'यहां' means this sign (Libra, Varuna's house); the sign is not named in this sentence.
classical_check: Agrees: an exalted Saturn gives strong results.

gist: Broken caption 'अब यह क्या है दास यह क्या है दिल अगर दिल से काम करे दास सोचो कितना सुख दे देगा वो आपको कोई सुख नहीं देगा': something about a servant and the heart giving happiness, but the sense is not recoverable.
Opening claim for a story: people happily believe that life will not go on without them.
Story of Mona: once she had a physical illness and cried to her women friends that she was ill and the house could not run if she was not there.
Mona lists what depends on her: no bread would be made, nobody would send the children to school, her mother-in-law is difficult, her husband cannot even make tea.
Her friends remind her that she once used the mother-in-law as an excuse for missing a function and school pick-up as an excuse for missing a party.
The friends say they would even welcome her at a family function with the children, if she would come along.
Mona refuses, saying she cannot leave the house alone, it is her responsibility, and nothing runs without her because nobody else knows how.
As her illness grew, poor Mona died, and her friends were saddened.
The friends wondered how her family must be managing but felt too awkward to ask.
Four friends together decide to phone Mona's husband Mangeram to ask if everything is all right and to express their sorrow.
A month, two months pass; after about four months they finally gather courage and phone him.
The phone rings unanswered; an hour later Mangeram calls back and apologises for not picking up.
The friends ask where he was and how he could be busy when they had called to offer condolence.
Mangeram replies that his phone was in the locker because he had come to play lawn tennis and meet friends.
He adds that he played billiards first, had a couple of drinks, then played tennis and left the phone away; the rest of his sentence is garbled.
Asked about the children, he says they have gone to school, no trouble, he has hired a servant who manages somehow.
For his old mother he has hired a maid who looks after her, and things are slowly returning to normal.
The friends are astonished that the house which could not run without Mona now runs without her; she had imagined herself to be God and was mistaken.
The children were brought up, a maid and a servant for food were hired, a nurse for the mother, and all the work gets done.
Moral of the story: you are not irreplaceable, life will not stop without you, and even the most helpless person's life goes on.

hindi: कौन चलाता है कौन चलाता है वरुण शनि तुके से चल रही है यह दोनों तुक्के के देवता है पता नहीं यार कैसे चल रही है साला तुक्के ही लगते जा रहे हैं
says: Who keeps life running? Varuna and Saturn: life goes on by tukka (luck, a fluke), and these two are the gods of flukes. Nobody knows how it runs, but the flukes keep landing.
cells_derived_method: none: a karaka statement, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'तुक्का' means a lucky guess or fluke; he uses it as a name for unexplained workings of life, not as an insult.
classical_check: Differs: classically Saturn is the karaka of delay, labour and obstacles, not luck; Neptune is not in the classical set.

hindi: तुको की ना कुछ होता ही नहीं ये तुक्के से जुगाड़ करते हैं यह हो गया शनि महाराज आप सोचते हो होएगा कुछ नहीं यह जुगाड़ कराता है
says: These two do not work by plan but by jugaad (improvised fixes) through flukes, and that is Saturn Maharaj: when you think nothing will happen, he gets a jugaad done and the matter works out.
cells_derived_method: none: a karaka description, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'तुको की ना कुछ होता ही नहीं' is garbled; it is read as 'nothing is done by the book with them'.
classical_check: Differs: in classical texts Saturn gives results slowly through effort and endurance, not improvised luck.

hindi: और कृपा मिलती है वरुण की कृपा से वरुण एक ऐसा देवता है जिसने कृपा देनी है आपको
says: Grace comes through Varuna's grace; Varuna is the deity whose job it is to give grace to you. He makes Neptune the source of the grace he has been talking about.
cells_derived_method: none: a karaka statement, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'वरुण' is Neptune in his scheme; the second 'कृपा' may be Varuna's own grace.

hindi: अगर उसने कुछ बनाना है तो आपके पास अकल आ जाएगी आप पढ़े हो चाहे नहीं हो आपके पास पैसा आ जाएगा आप अमीर हो के नहीं हो
says: If Varuna decides to make something of you, wisdom will come to you whether or not you are educated, and money will come whether or not you are already rich. His grace overrides education and wealth.
cells_derived_method: none: a general claim about Varuna's grace, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'उसने कुछ बनाना है' reads as 'he wants to make something of you', not a specific house result; this is a promise-style claim and is recorded as spoken.

hindi: यह कृपा कैसे मिलती है कृपा लेना बड़ा भारी चमत्कार है
says: How is this grace obtained? He answers that receiving grace is a very big miracle. It is something one must be fit to take, not something that comes as a matter of course.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: He asks the question and does not answer it here, moving to a story.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Asks how we get the lesson on receiving grace and announces story number two, which the audience will understand.
Story two: Mangeram works for a Seth, is very hardworking and genuine, with no idle talk, no fuss and no pleading.
The Seth thinks he is a good lad who works well, that he pays him little, and that he should give him more.
Next day Mangeram takes leave; the Seth is annoyed that he had just decided to raise the pay but decides to give it anyway.
The Seth raises Mangeram's pay; Mangeram takes the money and says nothing, and the Seth wishes he had at least said thank you.
The Seth grumbles that such people lack sense and live on employers' strength, treats the raise as a bonus, and work carries on for a while.
The Seth admits the pay was fair and the lad is fine, but when Mangeram takes leave again next day he calls him a shirker not worth the trouble; the story continues in the next slice.
Story two continues: the Seth rages that such people are scoundrels, you feed them and pay them and they feel nothing; Mangeram went on leave, so he will cut his bonus.
At next month's pay time the Seth gives no bonus and pays even less; Mangeram takes it again and just says fine.
The Seth fumes that Mangeram does not even speak, apologise or ask why the pay was reduced, and wonders if he is a donkey.
After five or six days the Seth reflects that he is a strange man with no fault in his work, and calls Mangeram over.
The Seth reminds him that he raised the pay with no thanks, then Mangeram took leave and the pay was cut, and still he did not plead: does he not value it?
Mangeram says what can he say, great is the grace of the Almighty; the Seth asks how, since he is a pauper, and Mangeram asks how he is a pauper.
Mangeram explains that on his first day of leave a son was born at his house; when the pay was raised he took it as coming from the baby's fortune, not his own.
Six months later his mother died in the village and he took leave to travel; the pay was cut next day and he took it as his mother's share of fortune leaving, so no matter.
The Seth asks if he thinks about nothing; Mangeram says one whose contract God has taken needs no thought, so he neither says yes or no, nor curses, cries, protests or begs.
The Seth says that from today Mangeram will be his successor.
Believe it, people do receive grace; this one was the story about money.
Stories of grace in matters of knowledge are found all over the world.

hindi: और एक कहानी कृपा कब होती है जब आप तटस्थ है जब आप सहज है और आप समर्पित है
says: Grace comes when you are neutral (tatastha, not swayed by gain or loss), at ease and natural (sahaj), and surrendered (samarpit). These three states are his condition for receiving grace.
cells_derived_method: none: a spiritual condition for grace, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'और एक कहानी' is a lead-in that is not followed by another story here; the sentence is read as a statement on when grace comes.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not list these three states as the condition for grace.

hindi: जिसका ठेका ही भगवान ने ले रखा है गुरु ने ले रखा है कृपा ने ले रखा है उनको कृपा मिलती है
says: Grace goes to those whose contract (thekaa, the responsibility for them) is held by God, the guru or grace itself. In his image, a person who has handed over the burden gets taken care of.
cells_derived_method: none: a spiritual principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'ठेका' means contract; it is the story's Mangeram line made into a rule.
classical_check: Silent: a devotional claim and not part of classical Jyotish.

hindi: सबसे पहले कृपा लो आपके ऊपर कृपा होगी आपकी वाणी में सरस्वती विराजमान हो जाएगी राहु बैठ जाएगा और आपके काम होंगे आप बोल दोगे किसी को वह आशीर्वाद लग जाएगा
says: First take grace; once grace is on you, Saraswati takes her seat in your speech, Rahu settles in, your works get done, and whatever you say to anyone works as a blessing. He makes grace the first thing, with powerful speech as its result.
cells_derived_method: Speech and the power of one's word are read from the 2nd house, so the meaning shifts with the sign and the planets on the 2nd; Rahu on it adds reach and persuasion.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Rahu in Gemini on the 2nd gives quick, persuasive and witty speech that carries weight; lagna Taurus.
Derived: Rahu in Sagittarius on the 2nd gives speech that sounds like a blessing or a teacher's pronouncement; lagna Scorpio.

ambiguity: 'राहु बैठ जाएगा' is unclear: it may mean Rahu is seated in the speech house, or that Rahu settles and stops troubling. Speech is mapped to the 2nd house only by derivation, not by him.
classical_check: Partly agrees: the 2nd house is classically speech and Rahu there gives forceful speech, but linking this to grace is his own.

gist: Many such people exist; people go to elders to ask for blessings, saying please bless us, say something, do this; nobody knows what is actually received.
Our usual problem is exactly this: abuse the one who cut the pay and flatter the one who raised it.
This reacting to gain and loss is the source of husband-wife quarrels and fights in every house.

hindi: यही बसर वर्क कर के आपने यह सीख लिया तो आपका वरुण प्रसन्न है
says: If you learn this steadiness in gain and loss through practice, your Varuna (Neptune) is pleased. He ties the neutral, surrendered attitude to a happy Varuna.
cells_derived_method: none: a statement tying an attitude to a planet, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'बसर वर्क' is garbled, read as 'by working on this'; 'प्रसन्न' (pleased) is his way of saying the planet gives its good result.
classical_check: Silent: Neptune is not classical.

gist: Rama example: your heart beats like Rama's, so if there is exile, no problem; Ravana died and they won, yet Rama said we only had to take Sita, Lanka is yours, keep it.

hindi: मर्यादा वरुण यहां रहता है
says: Maryada, living within dignified limits and keeping one's word, is where Varuna dwells. He places Neptune in the quality of restraint and propriety shown by Rama.
cells_derived_method: none: a karaka statement, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'यहां' points back to the Rama example; it is read as 'in this kind of conduct'.
classical_check: Silent: Neptune is not classical; Varuna as the upholder of rta and order is Vedic.

hindi: अगर आप इस नेचर के हैं आपका ग्रह ही ठीक है कुंडली में ऑटोमेटिक सही घर मिलेगा वास्तु वाला ऑटोमेटिक सही फैक्ट्री मिलेगी
says: If you are of this nature, your planet is fine in the chart, and you will automatically get the right house in the vastu sense and the right factory. A vastu-link claim: a settled planet brings suitable premises without effort.
cells_derived_method: Home and premises are read from the 4th house, a factory or workplace from the 10th and 4th; so the meaning follows the planet's house and sign, with strong placements delivering suitable premises.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: a settled planet on the 4th in Libra brings a balanced, well-proportioned home; lagna Cancer.
Derived: a settled planet on the 10th in Capricorn brings a sturdy, well-organised workplace or factory; lagna Aries.

ambiguity: 'आपका ग्रह' is not named; Varuna is assumed from the previous sentences. It is a promise-style claim and is recorded as spoken.
classical_check: Silent as a rule; classical Jyotish reads home from the 4th and work from the 10th but does not tie it to this attitude.

gist: Voice of the person with grace: there is nothing in these things, they are useless, why get stuck in such circles; we never did anything, we did not even get our charts matched.

hindi: कृपा है इस जन्म की या पूर्व जन्म की है किसी गुरु की है कृपा है
says: Such a person's good fortune without remedies or chart-matching is grace, whether from this birth, a previous birth or a guru. He names three sources of grace.
cells_derived_method: none: a statement on the source of grace, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: None; it answers the skeptic voice in the previous sentence.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical texts read past-life merit (purva punya) from the 5th and 9th houses; guru's grace is devotional.

gist: On the strength of that grace, the heart chakra and the root chakra (muladhara) get synchronised.
The muladhara is the whole Ramayana: everything is obtained from here and the things of the world are made from here; the two chakras are synchronised.
In such a state people see repeating numbers on the clock, 11:11, 12:12 and similar double numbers; nowadays this is called synchronicity.
When the root and heart chakras sync, signals come automatically from the cosmos and double numbers come into view, which means you are aligning with the cosmos.

hindi: अगर आपकी एलाइनमेंट हो रही है तो उसके लिए ग्रेट च्यूड रखो यानी शुकराना
says: If this alignment with the cosmos is happening, keep gratitude (shukrana) for it. His instruction to someone receiving signs is to stay thankful.
cells_derived_method: none: a general attitude remedy, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'ग्रेट च्यूड' is the English word gratitude as the caption wrote it.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not name gratitude as a remedy.

hindi: शुकराना इज नॉट शुक्र है भगवान तेरा शुक्र है भगवान तेरा नहीं आप 24 घंटे ग्रेटू में हो कि तेरा ही है तेरा ही है रा रा ते करके ही बात खत्म हो गई
says: Gratitude does not mean just saying thank you God; it means living in gratitude 24 hours a day, feeling that everything is yours (God's). When you reach this, the matter is settled.
cells_derived_method: none: a general attitude remedy, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: The end of the sentence 'रा रा ते करके ही बात खत्म हो गई' is garbled; read as 'with the feeling that all is Yours, the matter is finished'.
classical_check: Silent: classical texts do not describe gratitude in this way.

hindi: जब आप यह लेते हैं तो आपके पास अपने आप सही जोशी मिल जाता अपने आप बाबा मिल जाता है सड़क पर मिल जाता कोई हाथ देख के कहता बेटा तेरा ये होना है
says: When you take this grace, the right astrologer (joshi) or baba finds you by himself, even on the road, looks at your hand and tells you what is going to happen to you. Guidance reaches you without your searching for it.
cells_derived_method: none: a general claim about guidance arriving by grace, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: Joshi and baba here are popular terms for an astrologer or holy man met by chance.
classical_check: Silent: a devotional claim and not a classical rule.

hindi: वो अपने आप पता नहीं कैसे हो जाता है अगले को आता है कि नहीं आता आप ले लेते हो उससे
says: It all comes about by itself, nobody knows how; whether or not the other person really has the knowledge, you take from him what you need. The result does not depend on the guide being genuinely skilled.
cells_derived_method: none: a general claim about guidance arriving by grace, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: The sentence is loosely spoken; it is read as saying the outcome works through your openness and not the guide's skill.
classical_check: Silent: a devotional claim and not a classical rule.

hindi: यह तब है जब आपका वरुण और शनि सेट हो जाता है
says: All this, the grace and the right guidance arriving by itself, happens when your Varuna and Saturn are set, that is, settled and well placed. He makes the pair of Neptune and Saturn the condition for the grace to work.
cells_derived_method: Whether Neptune and Saturn are settled depends on sign and house: Saturn in Libra (exalted), Capricorn or Aquarius is settled; Neptune in a Mars sign is not, by his earlier rule.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Saturn exalted in Libra on the 7th is settled, helping the grace pattern in partnerships; lagna Aries.
Derived: Saturn debilitated in Aries on the 10th is not settled, so the grace pattern fails in career matters; lagna Cancer.

ambiguity: 'सेट' is not defined; read as 'well placed or settled' and not tied to a particular sign or house by him.
classical_check: Silent: Neptune is not classical; Saturn's strength by sign is classical.

hindi: बाकी ग्रह अपनी ही राशि के अनुसार उसी प्रकार से जो मित्र ग्रहों के हैं वही राशि के अनुसार फल देते हैं आपकी कॉन्शियस चेतना इसको जान के करेगी
says: The remaining planets give results according to the sign they are in, in the same way, with signs of friendly planets giving friendly results. Your conscious awareness will then act knowing this.
cells_derived_method: The result changes with the sign: own sign gives full, direct results, a friend's sign gives good support, an enemy's or debilitation sign gives strain, and the house sets the life area.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Mars in own sign Aries on the 1st gives full, direct results in self and vitality; lagna Aries.
Derived: Mars in the friendly sign of the Sun on the 10th gives good, authoritative results at work; lagna Scorpio.
Derived: Mars debilitated in Cancer on the 4th gives strained results at home and in emotional peace; lagna Aries.

ambiguity: The sentence is loosely spoken; it reads as sign-dignity based results for the other planets (not Neptune and Saturn). 'आपकी कॉन्शियस चेतना' is read as the listener's awareness.
classical_check: Agrees: results by own, friend, enemy and debilitation signs are the classical dignity rules.

hindi: और यह जान लो आपके कई उपाय फेल है अगर आपकी कुंडली कहती है यह होगा ही होकर रहेगा आप कुछ नहीं उखाड़ सकते
says: Know that many of your remedies fail if the chart says a thing will definitely happen; in that case you can do nothing about it. He admits fixed events in a chart that remedies cannot change.
cells_derived_method: none: a general claim about the limits of remedies, not dependent on house or sign as stated.
ambiguity: He does not say what in a chart makes an event fixed here; the next sentence points to retrograde planets.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical texts accept firm karma (dridha) results and limited remedy power; he states it more starkly.

hindi: इसके अंतर्गत एक बड़ा मेजर ड्रामा आता है फॉल्ट आती है ग्रहों की उस फॉल्ट का नाम है वक्री होना
says: Under this comes a major drama: a fault of the planets, and the name of that fault is being retrograde (vakri). He introduces retrogression as the planetary fault behind events that cannot be avoided.
cells_derived_method: none stated yet: he only names retrogression as the fault; its house and sign effects are not given in this sentence.
ambiguity: The sentence starts at the end of one slice and finishes in the next; whether all retrograde planets or only some are meant is not said yet.
classical_check: Partly agrees: retrograde planets are classically strong in cheshta bala and can give delayed or intense results; calling it a fault is his own framing.

gist: First audience question: all successful people say in interviews that they maintained discipline, hard work and consistency, but you say these things belong to another domain; the caption is garbled at the end.

hindi: तो सारे सफल लोग कभी ना कभी पिटते हैं क्या बदला बहुत डिसिप्लिन किया कोहली ने रोहित शर्मा ने पिट रहे हैं आजकल समय की मार है कुछ नहीं है
says: His answer: even successful people get beaten at some time, and the question is what changed; Kohli and Rohit Sharma had plenty of discipline and are being beaten these days, which is just the blow of time and nothing else. He puts success and failure on time and not on discipline. Real people are named only as his examples.
cells_derived_method: none: a general claim about time, not dependent on house or sign as stated; which period is good or bad would come from the dasha lord and transits.
ambiguity: 'समय की मार' means the blow of time; he does not name a dasha or planet for the named persons.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: classical Jyotish makes dasha and transit timing decide results beyond effort, but it does not say effort is irrelevant.

hindi: यह अहंकार बोलता है मैंने किया डिसिप्लिन क्याय
says: It is the ego that says 'I did it by discipline'; he questions what discipline, since time was doing the work. He calls claiming credit for success the ego speaking.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'क्याय' is read as 'what discipline?'.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: अरे टाइम है रॉकेट की तरह छाए हुए हो जब टाइम बुरा आएगा तुम्हारे नाम की स्पेलिंग भी वही होगी तुम भी वही होगे तुम पिट जाओगे सब टाइम है
says: It is only time: when the time is good you blaze like a rocket, but when a bad time comes your name's spelling will be the same and you will be the same person, and you will be beaten. The person does not change, only the time does.
cells_derived_method: Whether a period is a rocket or a beating is read from the dasha lord by its house and sign strength: an exalted or own-sign lord in a good house lifts, a debilitated lord in a hard house brings reversals.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Jupiter's period with Jupiter exalted in Cancer on the 10th is a rocket-like rise in career; lagna Libra.
Derived: Saturn's period with Saturn debilitated in Aries on the 8th is a beating time with sudden reversals; lagna Virgo.

ambiguity: The cause of the good and bad time is not named here; dasha is inferred from 'टाइम'.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit: the vimshottari dasha period is the classical measure of good and bad times.

hindi: टाइम कौन है टाइम सबसे बड़ी करेंसी है
says: Who is Time? Time is the biggest currency of all, more valuable than money. He sets up time as what everything is paid in.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: None.
classical_check: Silent.

gist: Auto-rickshaw illustration: time is eaten, so give the auto driver the extra fare, otherwise you must wait fifteen or twenty minutes; the caption of the amount is garbled.

hindi: ग्रह टाइम चूसता है आपका
says: A planet sucks your time: what an afflicting planet takes from you is time, in the form of delay and a longer bad period. It is his short definition of how planets hurt.
cells_derived_method: none: a general statement about planets, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: No planet is named; it applies to any troubling planet.
classical_check: Partly agrees: classical texts describe delay and obstruction from malefics, but not as taking time.

hindi: एक महीने में वायरल फीवर ठीक हो जाएगा बिना दवाई के भी दवाई दो चढ़ावा दो डॉक्टर का पैसा दो काम करो एक्सरसाइज करो आराम जो जो करना है पा दिन में ठीक हो जाएगा टाइम बचाओ
says: His analogy: a viral fever will pass in a month even without medicine, but with medicine, offerings, the doctor's fee, activity, exercise and rest it clears in about five days, so spend to save time. The planetary remedy likewise buys back time with money and effort. The fever example is only his analogy, not medical advice.
cells_derived_method: none: a general remedy rationale, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'पा दिन' is a cut-off number of days, read as about five; 'चढ़ावा' means an offering at a shrine.
classical_check: Silent as stated; the idea that remedies shorten a bad period is common in remedial Jyotish.

hindi: टाइम टाइम सबसे ज्यादा बलवान है राम और कृष्ण भी 12 पर नहीं बदल सके
says: Time is the most powerful thing of all; even Ram and Krishna could not change it at the 12. He claims time overrides even the avatars.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: '12 पर' is unclear: it may refer to the 12 years of exile, the 12th house, or a clock hour; no cell is recorded.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: टाइम इज द ओनली थिंग क्योंकि टाइम की करेंसी टाइम ही परमात्मा है
says: Time is the only real thing, because the currency is time and time itself is the Supreme (Paramatma). He equates time with God.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: The phrase 'टाइम की करेंसी टाइम ही परमात्मा है' is run together; read as 'time is the currency, and time is God'.
classical_check: Partly agrees: Kala (time) is a deity in Vedic thought and the Kalapurusha is the cosmic person in Jyotish.

hindi: टाइम के ऊपर ही तो सारे फोस फोर्थ डायमेंशन है ही स्पेस टाइम की स्पेस में है टाइम टाइम टाइम की बात है
says: Everything rests on time: all the force, the fourth dimension, and even space lies within time's space; in the end it is all a matter of time. A physics-style way of saying time is the base of all.
cells_derived_method: none: a general principle, not dependent on house or sign.
ambiguity: 'फोस' is garbled, probably 'फोर्स' or 'फ़ोर्स'; the grammar is loose, so the exact claim about space and time is uncertain.
classical_check: Silent: a modern-physics gloss.

gist: Remarks that they have already covered a class on space-time earlier.
Audience question: Sir, you often talk about movies in your videos; can one plan like the Professor in Money Heist and succeed, and how does one plan like him?

Begins his answer with a digression: that would take a whole class; Money Heist is a very good serial everyone should watch, with a character called the Professor; the sentence is cut off at the slice end.
Describes the Professor from the Money Heist series: he plans a robbery and then carries it out calmly and with enjoyment.
Through the whole series dozens of troubles hit the Professor and every plan carries the fear of being caught, yet he just says let us see and never loses his cool.
Asks what losing cool means and answers that it is dropping into a begging attitude; the Professor does not ask God for help (caption around 'नीचे के चक्कर' is unclear).
Bluntly dismisses asking God for things: no need to ask because God is already with you and you are alive because of Him.

hindi: जो तुम्हारे अंदर एनर्जी बॉडी है उसी से चिजी बॉडी चल रही है
says: The energy body inside you is what keeps the physical body running, so being alive is itself the sign that the divine energy is already within you.
ambiguity: 'चिजी बॉडी' is a caption slip, almost certainly 'फिजिकल बॉडी'. He does not say which planet or house stands for the energy body here.
classical_check: Close to the Vedantic idea of subtle (sukshma) and gross (sthula) bodies, with prana animating the gross one; Jyotish texts are silent.

hindi: भगवान को तुम दफा करो ना करो भगवान नहीं अच्छा बुरा मानता वो तो बेवकूफ है स्कूल गया हुआ बच्चा है कि हां जी भगवान बुरा भी मानता है अच्छा भी
says: God does not take offence or feel pleased by what you do, whether you push Him away or not; only a foolish schoolchild believes God minds good or bad behaviour.
ambiguity: 'भगवान को दफा करो' is rude slang for dismissing God; he means the choice does not change God's attitude. The last words 'अच्छा भी' are cut off.
classical_check: Agrees with Gita 5.15, where the Lord takes neither the sin nor the merit of anyone; Jyotish texts still prescribe propitiation remedies, so the written tradition is not uniform.

hindi: ये कहने की बात है भगवान सजा देगा भगवान मजा देगा भगवान कुछ नहीं देता
says: Sayings such as 'God will punish' or 'God will give you pleasure' are only manners of speech; God hands out nothing, and results come from the person's own action.
ambiguity: 'मजा देगा' may be 'maza chakhayega' (will make you taste fun or consequence); either way the meaning is that God is not the dispenser.
classical_check: Consistent with the karma-phala doctrine, but conflicts with the many remedy chapters in BPHS that ask the deity to remove past-karma afflictions.

hindi: भगवान कहता है सरवाइव करो यह पड़ा है रेस्टोरेंट में सब पड़ा है जो लेना है ले लो
says: Restaurant analogy: all that God asks is that you survive; the world is like a restaurant with everything laid out, and you may take whatever you wish.
ambiguity: 'सरवाइव' is English 'survive'; he is giving free choice of action, not saying anything about luck.
classical_check: Echoes the Gita idea of free action with fruit following; the restaurant image is his own and not classical.

hindi: जो करोगे उसके बदले रेसिप प्रोकेन होगी आपको उसके बदले वैसा ही फलित मिलेगा अपने आप जो चीज उठाओगे स्टोर से उसके उतने पैसे लगेंगे कर्म की कीमत
says: Law of reciprocity: whatever you do comes back to you in the same kind, automatically, like a store where each item you pick up has a price; that price is the cost of karma.
ambiguity: 'रेसिप प्रोकेन' is caption noise for 'reciprocation' or 'reciprocal'.
classical_check: Agrees with the classical karma-phala rule that action returns as like fruit; silent on how the chart shows the price.

hindi: इसलिए सड़ कोड़ो मत बढ़िया-बढ़िया चीजें उठाओ यह आपके अपने ऊपर है
says: Because every pick has a price, do not choose rotten items from the shelf; pick good ones, since the choice of what to do is yours alone.
ambiguity: 'सड़ कोड़ो' is probably 'सड़ी-गली' (rotten, spoiled); the shelf stands for kinds of action.
classical_check: Agrees with the general dharma advice to choose good action; Jyotish texts are silent on this exact framing.

gist: After making a plan do not lose your cool: if abuse or taunts can shake you, you are sitting in another person's pocket and are no Professor.
Host says yes and moves to the next question.
Question read out: in class we say there is no need to worship a stone idol, but after pran pratishtha (consecration) can the idol be worshipped?

hindi: आपको पूजा पाठ करने की जरूरत इसलिए नहीं है क्योंकि आप थोड़े टाइम पूजा करके आवाहन करोगे देवता का
says: Begins his answer: ritual worship is not needed by someone who can connect directly, because a puja only invokes the deity for a short while.
ambiguity: The sentence is rushed and the reason is only implied; it reads as 'puja gives only temporary invocation, a lasting connection comes another way', which the next sentence completes.
classical_check: Differs from the Agama and Puranic stress on daily worship (nitya puja) as a duty; Jyotish texts silent on this view.

hindi: जो लोग परमानेंट जानते हैं वो वाली बात है कि संत ने कुटिया में बैठ कर के वही बैठ के ध्यान के द्वारा परमात्मा एनर्जी बॉडी को पकड़ लिया
says: People who know the permanent way work like the saint who sits in a hut and, by meditation alone, catches hold of the Paramatma (supreme) energy body, with no idol or ritual.
ambiguity: The sentence continues into the next caption line, which says the saint 'was already connected'.
classical_check: Agrees with the yogic and Upanishadic path of direct meditation; Jyotish texts are silent.

hindi: पकड़ी पकड़ाई है उससे कनेक्टेड है और व उससे जानकारी में कनेक्ट हो गया परमात्मा ने तो हमारे अंदर सांस लेना छोड़ा नहीं है हम भूल जाते हैं
says: The link with the Paramatma already exists, since it never stopped our breathing; the saint only became consciously aware of it, while ordinary people forget it.
ambiguity: 'जानकारी में कनेक्ट' means knowingly or consciously connected; the caption has no punctuation so the speaker change to 'we' is soft.
classical_check: Matches the Vedantic view that the Self is always present and only awareness is missing; silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: लेकिन आम व्यक्ति को समझ नहीं आता तो व क्या करता है कहता मूर्ति लाओ कहीं मूर्ति है रही
says: An ordinary person cannot grasp this subtle connection, so tradition gives him an idol as a visible support to hold on to.
ambiguity: 'मूर्ति है रही' is garbled; read as 'an idol is kept (somewhere)'.
classical_check: Agrees with the Puranic and Bhakti explanation of murti as an aid for those not yet able to meditate on the formless; silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: अब उस मूर्ति को चार्ज किया जा सकता उससे ऊपर की श्रेणी के लोगों के लिए उसमें देवता का मंत्र द्वारा आवाहन करके
says: For people one class above the ordinary, the idol can be charged by calling the deity into it with mantra.
ambiguity: 'उससे ऊपर की श्रेणी' could mean a higher class of seekers or a higher class of idol; the reading used is the first.
classical_check: Agrees with Agama practice of avahana and pran pratishtha of the deity into the image; silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: जो कॉस्मिक एनर्जी है वो वाइब्रेशन पर चलती है स्ट्रिंग थ्योरी ये कहती है कि आप हर चीज एक वाइब्रेशन ही है कोई चीज ऐसी नहीं है
says: Cosmic energy works through vibration, and he cites string theory to say that everything is only vibration; he uses this as the physical basis for how mantras can act.
ambiguity: He states string theory as settled fact; the sentence is cut off after 'कोई चीज ऐसी नहीं है' and is finished in the next line.
classical_check: Not a Jyotish claim; the idea of sound as the root of creation is Vedic and Tantric (shabda or nada Brahman), while string theory is an unconfirmed physics hypothesis.

hindi: इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रोटॉन न्यूट्रॉन जो है क्वेक्स है वो नीचे क्वांटम फिजिक्स के अंदर बिल्कुल छोटे मैन्यूट पर जाते तो एक स्ट्रिंग्स की तरह धागे हैं जो वाइब्रेट कर रहे हैं
says: Physics support for the idea: electrons, protons, neutrons and quarks, looked at at the very smallest scale, are string-like threads that are vibrating.
ambiguity: 'क्वेक्स' is 'quarks' and 'मैन्यूट' is 'minute' (tiny) in the caption; protons and neutrons are made of quarks, so he lists levels together.
classical_check: Not a Jyotish claim; in physics, string theory is a proposal and has not been confirmed, so this is his analogy and not evidence.

hindi: स्ट्रिंग थ्योरी के अनुसार वो वाइब्रेशंस मंत्रों के द्वारा जिसने वेद वेद पाठी ने ज्ञानी ने जान ली उसके द्वारा वो देवता का आ वाहन करता है स्पेसिफिक एनर्जी का और उस मूर्ति में प्रतिष्ठित करता है
says: Mantras are those vibrations; a Veda-reciting scholar who really knows them uses mantra to call a specific deity-energy and then to install it in the idol.
ambiguity: 'आ वाहन' is the split spelling of 'आवाहन' (invocation); the sentence ends 'by mantra' in the next words.
classical_check: Agrees with the Agama and Vedic procedure of avahana followed by pran pratishtha by a qualified priest; Jyotish texts silent.

hindi: अब वो मूर्ति उसका पोर्टल बन गई है वाया जा सकते हैं वाया वाया जा सकते हैं आपने आप आवाज लगाते
says: After consecration the idol becomes a portal to that deity-energy, a route through which you can reach it; he starts to explain it with the example of calling someone by voice.
ambiguity: 'वाया' is English 'via'; the calling example is completed in the next caption line.
classical_check: Agrees with the Agamic idea that the consecrated image is a seat (adhishthana) of the deity; silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: हैं हेलो मांगेराम हेलो अब सुन लिया अब मांगेराम दूर है आप फोन उठाते हो बीच में फोन के थ्रू बात करते हो तो फोन चार्जड है ऐसे वो देवता की मूर्ति प्रतिष्ठित हो गई
says: Phone analogy: if Mangeram is near you shout and he hears; if he is far you speak through a charged phone; the consecrated idol is that charged phone connecting you to a distant deity.
ambiguity: 'मांगेराम' is just a made-up name for the person being called.
classical_check: The phone image is his own; the underlying idea of the image as a channel to the deity matches Agama tradition, and Jyotish texts are silent.

hindi: अब आप उसके ऊपर के कॉन्शसनेस के लेवल पर जब जाते हो तो उस देवता का घर बैठे आवान कर सकते हो
says: At a higher level of consciousness you can invoke that same deity from your home seat without needing the idol.
ambiguity: 'आवान' is a caption slip for 'आवाहन'; 'घर बैठे' means sitting at home, with no instrument.
classical_check: Agrees with the graded path in Hindu tradition from image worship to mental worship (manasa puja); silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: और जब वह चीज भी आगे निकल जाती है तो आप उस देवता को अपने अंदर ही आवाहन कर सकते हो यह आपके ऊपर है
says: Beyond that stage you can invoke the deity inside yourself, and which stage you work at is your own choice.
ambiguity: 'वह चीज' refers to the home-invocation stage just mentioned.
classical_check: Agrees with the top rung of the graded worship ladder (internal worship); silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: इसलिए प्राण प्रतिष्ठित मर्ता की मूर्ति की पूजा करो उसका लफड़ा य है उस मूर्ति को खाली नहीं छोड़ सकते रात को अकेला नहीं छोड़ सकते घर में होना चाहिए कोई अनअटेंडेड नहीं छोड़ सकते देवता को
says: So worship a consecrated idol, but with a catch: it cannot be left empty or alone, above all at night; someone has to be in the house, since a deity cannot be left unattended.
ambiguity: None; the sentence is clear apart from the colloquial 'लफड़ा' (trouble or catch).
classical_check: Agrees with Agama and domestic-worship custom that an installed deity needs regular daily seva; Jyotish texts silent.

hindi: फिर यह नहीं होगा कि हा सारी फैमिली मसूरी जा रही है घूमने आप देवता को आवाहन करके बैठे हो उसे छोड़ नहीं सकते
says: Practical result of that rule: a family that has installed a deity cannot all go off on holiday together (his example is Mussoorie), because the deity cannot be left behind.
ambiguity: He does not say how long an absence is allowed; the rule is stated for an overnight or whole-family absence.
classical_check: Consistent with the custom of arranging a substitute for daily seva when away; Jyotish texts silent.

gist: A listener says the idol is a portal and an energy field so someone is present there anyway; he answers yes, that presence is there.
Repeats that a consecrated idol, wherever it is placed, cannot remain unattended.
Question: if an actor, feeling it deeply, gives a wrong command while acting, will it be fulfilled?

hindi: ओ यस तो व पूरी होगी और य बिल्कुल होगी रॉन्ग कमांड देके अगर दे दे कमांड को एक्टिंग करते समय
says: Answers yes: a wrong or negative command spoken with real feeling gets fulfilled, even when it was spoken during acting.
ambiguity: The caption is broken; he may mean the command is fulfilled only when it is felt, which the next sentence qualifies.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit with the Vedic belief in the power of spoken word (vak siddhi, 'tathastu'); Jyotish texts are silent on actors.

hindi: एक्टिंग करते समय अगर उसको पता है तो एक्टिंग है लेकिन अगर वैसे ही बोल दे
says: Qualifier: if the actor is aware that it is only acting, it stays acting; but if the line slips out naturally, as if meant, the command takes effect.
ambiguity: The sentence stops before the result is stated; the result (it works if said naturally) is inferred from the example that follows.
classical_check: Silent; this is his own rule of thumb about awareness and speech.

gist: Example of a named film actor who casually said he would exercise in a wheelchair at 86; he says it was said very naturally and no one knows if his legs will suffer, time will tell (speculation about a named person's health, not recorded as a rule).
Listener says the cord-cutting exercise can be taken at the end; he agrees to do it last and finish the rest first.
Question: if taking blessings while doing remedies makes everything right, why do karma at all, since everyone will just seek grace.
Restates the question with amusement: if after a remedy karma is thrown aside and all is fixed anyway, then people will do only remedies and need no karma.

hindi: मैं शत प्रतिशत एग्री करता हूं इस बात से
says: He agrees one hundred percent with the objection, meaning that remedies or grace alone cannot replace one's own action.
ambiguity: It is not fully clear whether he agrees that remedies make karma unnecessary or agrees that remedies alone should not be relied on; the rest of the passage supports the second.
classical_check: Agrees with the classical teaching that remedies reduce difficulty but purushartha (effort) is still needed; BPHS and Phaladeepika remedies are given as aids.

hindi: अपने जीवन में बहुत एक्सपेरिमेंट कर कर के धक्के खा खू के रोटी भी खाई पर उसके बाद ये रिलाइज किया कि कुछ मत करो करो होने प डालो
says: From his own experience: after many experiments, hard knocks and earning a living, he came to the view that one should not run after doing things and should leave it to what is happening.
ambiguity: 'करो होने पर डालो' is unclear; read as 'leave it to what is happening'. It could also be 'put it on happening' in the sense of surrendering to events.
classical_check: Differs from the BPHS and Phaladeepika practice of prescribing active remedies; closer to the Gita idea of surrender after action.

hindi: कैसे करो ऐसा यार कुछ उपाय कर लो फिर क्या करो फिर कुछ समझ लो दान दया की कहानियां फिर क्या करो कृपा लेने के लिए पैर पूर दाब लो फिर क्या करो कुछ वास्तु वास्तु सेट कर लो
says: He lists the ladder of things people try in turn: some remedy, then charity and compassion stories, then pressing the feet of elders or gurus for grace, then vastu corrections, asking 'then what?' after each.
ambiguity: 'पैर पूर दाब लो' is probably 'pair daab lo' (press the feet). He lists these as things that do not finally settle the matter, not as his own advice.
classical_check: Daan, seva and vastu are all standard Jyotish and Vastu remedies; his view that they do not end the matter differs from the texts.

hindi: फिर क्या करो कुछ मत करो फिर अपने आप हो रहा है
says: The last rung of the ladder: do nothing, because things are already happening by themselves.
ambiguity: He means do not chase remedies; he does not mean give up work, as the next sentence shows.
classical_check: Differs from the remedy chapters of BPHS; close to the Gita idea of letting fruit unfold after action.

hindi: फिर जो हो रहा है उसमें कर्म करते रहो सब सही हो रहा है
says: Then, inside whatever is unfolding, keep doing your own karma (effort) and trust that all of it is happening rightly.
ambiguity: None; this is the counterpart of the previous sentence (no remedy-chasing, but continued effort).
classical_check: Agrees with the Gita teaching of doing action without worry over fruit.

gist: Personal remark that apart from this he does nothing else and that he has been working for nearly four decades of his life.
Garbled line 'अब तो आजकल बातें होने लगी तो इसलिए बोल देते हैं हम मैंने कुछ नहीं किया': roughly 'nowadays people talk, so I say I did nothing', but the link to the argument cannot be recovered.

hindi: लोगों को मना करता हूं मत करो ये उपाय करो तुम्हारा होएगा फिर अपने आप होने लगता है
says: He tells people to stop chasing remedies of the 'do this and it will happen' kind; once they stop, things begin to happen on their own.
ambiguity: 'ये उपाय करो तुम्हारा होएगा' could be a quote of the promise he refuses to make or an instruction he gives; the nearby 'do nothing' theme supports the first reading.
classical_check: Differs from BPHS, Phaladeepika and Lal Kitab, which prescribe specific remedies for specific afflictions.

hindi: फिर जब होने लगता है उसके लिए आप कर्म करो हिलो डलो बाकी हो रहा है अपने आप ही एडमिशन हो
says: Once things start moving you must still act and move about, and the rest unfolds by itself; his example, cut off at the end of the caption, is a child's admission happening.
ambiguity: The sentence is cut at 'एडमिशन हो', so the example is incomplete; it is probably about a child's admission to a school or college.
classical_check: Agrees with the classical pairing of daiva (fate) and purushartha (effort); silent on this example.

hindi: रहे हैं अपने आप जॉब लग रही है अपने आप काम हो रहे हैं अपने आप
says: Finishing the previous thought: when you stop chasing, admissions, jobs and tasks start happening on their own.
ambiguity: The sentence starts mid-way from the previous caption line (about an admission happening).
classical_check: Silent; this is his experience-based claim, close to the idea of daiva (fate) unfolding on its own.

hindi: पर उसके लिए सारे उपाय चाहिए खुद क्या करो कुछ नहीं
says: For that self-running flow all the remedies are still needed; as for what you yourself should do, he says nothing.
ambiguity: 'उसके लिए सारे उपाय चाहिए' may be a question put by a listener (do all remedies need doing?) and not his claim; read as his position because he goes on to say the remedies are the only thing to do.
classical_check: Agrees with the texts on giving remedies; the 'do nothing yourself' part is his own and differs from classical stress on effort.

hindi: कृष्ण जी ने क्या किया कुछ नहीं लेकिन रथ चलाया अरे वो बेकार की बहस है अरे उतना तो करेंगे ही
says: Krishna did nothing yet drove the chariot; he calls the argument over how much is doing and how much is not-doing a useless debate, since the small doing will be done anyway.
ambiguity: 'कुछ नहीं' is relative: Krishna drove the chariot, so the claim is about not owning the result, not about total inaction.
classical_check: Consistent with Gita on action without attachment to fruit; Jyotish texts silent.

hindi: लेकिन करना वो हो रहा है कृष्ण का तो मुकाबला नहीं कर सकते
says: The doing is being done through the divine; no human can compete with Krishna's will, so the 'I do' feeling is misplaced.
ambiguity: 'करना वो हो रहा है' is compressed; read as 'the doing is itself a happening'.
classical_check: Echoes Gita 18.61 (the Lord moves all beings as if on a machine); silent in Jyotish texts.

hindi: उसकी बुद्धि से मत चलो अर्जुन तू क्या कर तू भी कुछ मत कर तू सिर्फ बांड चला एक स्पेसिफिक काम फालतू नहीं करना ऐड ऑन नहीं बाकी मैं करूंगा
says: Voicing Krishna to Arjuna: do not run on your own intellect; do only your one specific task (shoot the arrow), add no extras, and the rest I will do.
ambiguity: 'उसकी बुद्धि' is odd (his intellect); it is probably Krishna's advice not to follow one's own mind. 'बांड' is caption noise for 'बाण' (arrow).
classical_check: Reflects the Gita teaching of doing one's own duty and surrendering the rest; this retelling is his own paraphrase.

hindi: यानी बाकी के उपाय कर लो और कुछ करने की जरूरत नहीं है फिर अपने आप होएगा
says: Conclusion: do the prescribed remedies, need nothing further, and the result will then come by itself.
ambiguity: 'बाकी के उपाय' may mean the remaining remedies or all the other remedies; either way he restricts the person's own doing to the remedy.
classical_check: Agrees with the Jyotish practice of prescribing remedies for afflictions; the 'nothing more needed' part is his own claim.

hindi: वो तुम करोगे ही जब तुम्हारे पर डंडा पड़ेगा और होने के लिए हालात बनेंगी तो तुम करोगे ही वो कर होना करवा रहा है तुमसे तुम खुद जाके ढूंढ रहे हो
says: You will act anyway when the stick falls and circumstances form; it is the happening that makes you do it, even when you think you are going out and searching on your own.
ambiguity: 'वो कर होना करवा रहा है' is garbled; read as 'it is the happening that is making you do it'.
classical_check: Agrees with the fatalistic reading of prarabdha where events shape action; classical texts also allow purushartha.

hindi: अब मैं शेयर मार्केट में पैसे लगा दूं नो लुट जाओगे अगर सूट नहीं करता
says: Investment remark, flagged: asked whether to put money into the share market, he says no, you will be ruined if it does not suit you (his statement, not recorded as advice or an engine rule).
ambiguity: He does not say what makes the market suit or not suit; 'सूट नहीं करता' is left to the chart.
classical_check: Jyotish texts judge speculation from the 5th, 8th and 11th houses; he gives no such test here.

hindi: अगर होने वाले ग्रहों को ऑन करते हो यानी कृपा लेते हो उपाय कर लेते हो को ससी तरह का ग्रह की करेक्ट तो आपके पास अपने आप ही काम आएगा
says: If you switch on the planets that are due to act, by taking grace and doing the remedy of the right planet, then work will come to you by itself.
ambiguity: 'को ससी तरह का ग्रह की करेक्ट' is garbled; read as 'the correct kind of planet's remedy'. 'होने वाले ग्रहों' may mean the planets whose period is about to run.
classical_check: Agrees in general with planet-wise remedies in BPHS; the 'switch on' wording is his own.

hindi: अपने आप ही कोई आके शेर बता जाएगा दादा जीी मर जाएंगे तुम्हारे लिए इसके शेर छोड़ गए अपने आप ही होगा
says: Example of an unasked windfall: someone will come and tell you that a grandfather has died leaving shares in your name, and it all happens by itself (an illustration, not a prediction of anyone's death or an investment tip).
ambiguity: 'शेर' is the caption spelling of 'शेयर'. The death of the grandfather is a made-up example.
classical_check: Silent; inheritance is read from the 8th house and the 2nd in classical texts, which he does not mention here.

hindi: फिर तुम करो जाओ पेपर वर्क साइन करो जाकर कर कर आ गओ हुई चीज पर करना नहीं हम खुद कर रहे हैं यह दो अलग बातें हैं
says: Once the thing has already happened you do the paperwork and sign; doing on an event that has occurred is a different matter from believing that you yourself are making it happen.
ambiguity: The sentence runs across the caption break and the middle part 'कर कर आ गओ' is garbled.
classical_check: Silent; this is his own way of separating karma-as-doing from prarabdha-as-happening.

hindi: इसलिए किस्मत ठीक करो डॉक्टर क्या कहता है ऐसे करो वैसे करो नहीं यह दो गोली यहां खा दो गोली वहां खा और पड़ जा
says: Therefore fix your fortune the way a patient follows a doctor: do not invent your own methods, take the prescribed pills at the right times and rest, meaning follow the remedy given and do nothing clever on top.
ambiguity: 'ऐसे करो वैसे करो नहीं' reads as the doctor not giving elaborate instructions; the doctor is only an analogy for the astrologer.
classical_check: Silent; the doctor analogy for remedies is his own.

gist: Mocks a yoga teacher's strict regimen: samosa out, kachori out, relief that golgappa did not come in between, wake at 4, sleep at 7, drink this decoction, do this and that yoga.

hindi: बंदा ठीक करना ही नहीं ना कुछ होने पर डाल दिया
says: The point of the regimen joke: such a person is not fixing himself through his own doing and has left the result to what happens.
ambiguity: Very compressed; it could instead mean the man is not meant to be fixed at all. The reading used follows the do-versus-happen theme.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: यह बहुत गुथी हुई कहानी है करना और होना ये हम सोचते हैं इसम क्लास हुई पड़ी करना और होना
says: The relation between doing and happening is a very tangled story; he says people think they understand it but the whole class gets lost in it.
ambiguity: 'इसम क्लास हुई पड़ी' is garbled; read as 'the class is stuck in this'.
classical_check: Silent; the free-will versus fate puzzle is old (purushartha and daiva) and texts do not settle it.

gist: Question: do people who fear dogs or cats, or have a phobia, have it because of Ketu or because of some other planet?

hindi: डॉग हो गया हमारा केतु कैट हो गए राहु उनसे डरते हैं तो कर
says: Animal karakas: the dog is Ketu and the cat is Rahu, so fear of dogs points to Ketu and fear of cats points to Rahu.
ambiguity: 'तो कर' at the end is cut off and continues into the next line; the phobia remedy comes in the next row.
classical_check: Dog is classically linked to Ketu; the cat-Rahu link is not a standard text assignment, so this part is his own.

hindi: लो फोबिया फोबिया क्या करें दवाई सवाई ले लो इसके लिए होम्योपैथिक मेडिसिन ले लो चंद्रमा का करेक्शन कर लो
says: For a phobia he suggests taking homeopathic medicine, which he treats as the way to correct the Moon (a health-remedy claim, not medical advice or a diagnosis).
ambiguity: The previous row says dog fear is Ketu and cat fear Rahu, yet the remedy is given through the Moon; he does not explain why, possibly because the Moon rules the mind and fear.
classical_check: Moon as mind (manas karaka) is classical; linking homeopathy to the Moon is his own scheme.

hindi: होम्योपैथिक मेडिसिन चंद्रमा जिसका कुंडली फेवर करती है कैसे करती है क्या नहीं करती यह सब बातें समझने में बहुत टाइम लगेगा पर यदि चंद्रमा फेवर करता है खुद रीड कर लो आप होम्योपैथिक मेडिसिन से ठीक होंगे
says: Homeopathy belongs to the Moon and works for a person whose chart favours the Moon; how to judge that takes long to explain, but if the Moon is favourable you will be cured by it (health claim, flagged, not advice).
cells_derived_method: Whether the Moon favours the chart is read from its sign dignity (Taurus exalted, Cancer own, Scorpio debilitated) and its house (kendra and trikona help, 6th, 8th and 12th hurt). He gives no test here; this is my reading from classical strength logic.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Moon exalted in Taurus in the 10th house, lagna Leo; Moon looks favourable, so homeopathy would be the system that suits this person.
Derived: Moon debilitated in Scorpio in the 6th house, lagna Gemini; Moon looks unfavourable, so by his logic homeopathy would not suit.

ambiguity: 'फेवर' is not defined: it could mean strong, well-placed, or simply benefic to the lagna.
classical_check: Moon's strength rules are classical; the Moon-homeopathy link is his own.

hindi: अब ट यूनिवर्सिटी कहेगी डॉक्टर कह रहे होमोपैथिक बहुत गंदी चीज है अब ट्राई करके देख लो ट्राई ट्राई में खेल लो ट्राई मना करते हैं वैसे ट्राई में देख लो लग गई तो चंद्रमा का फायदा हो रहा है
says: Trial test: even if university doctors dismiss homeopathy, just try it; if it works for you, that shows the Moon is helping you.
ambiguity: 'ट्राई मना करते हैं वैसे' is garbled; probably a remark that he does not normally advise trying things.
classical_check: Silent; using a remedy's success to infer the planet's favour is his own empirical test.

hindi: य चंद्रमा होमोपैथी ठीक करेगी आपको इस चक्कर में मत रहो कृपा कहीं से भी लो
says: Do not get stuck on which system will cure you; take grace (help) from wherever it comes.
ambiguity: The first part reads like a listener-style doubt about whether the Moon or homeopathy will do the cure, and he sets it aside.
classical_check: Silent.

hindi: नो नहीं बोलता कृपा लेने वाला आदमी वो कुत्ते से भी कृपा लेता है बिल्ली से भी
says: A person who knows how to receive grace never refuses it; he accepts help even from a dog or a cat.
ambiguity: Planets are not named; Ketu and Rahu are listed only because the dog and the cat were assigned to them a moment earlier.
classical_check: Silent; feeding dogs for Ketu is a common remedy, but receiving grace from them is his phrasing.

hindi: हमारे सनातन में कहा गया पेड़ का भी आशीर्वाद लो उसमें भी जीवन है उसम भगवान जान लो
says: Sanatan teaching, he says, is to take the blessing even of a tree, because it has life and God is in it.
ambiguity: None; 'जान लो' is an imperative: know that God is in it.
classical_check: Agrees with the Hindu reverence for trees such as peepal and tulsi; no specific Jyotish rule.

hindi: मेडिसिन मंगल के लिए एलोपैथिक बुध होगा आपका बढ़िया आयुर्वेदिक
says: Mapping of medicine systems to planets: allopathy goes with Mars and Ayurveda with Mercury, so Ayurveda is good if Mercury is your strong planet (health-remedy claim, flagged).
ambiguity: The sentence is compressed; 'बुध होगा आपका' means if Mercury is yours (strong).
classical_check: Silent; classical texts link Mars to surgery and Mercury to skin and nerves, but not to medicine systems.

hindi: बुध खराब है आयुर्वेदिक हेल्प कभी नहीं करेगा मंगल खराब है एलोपैथिक कुछ नहीं करेगा ऑपरेशन करना पड़ेगा चंद्रमा खराब है होमोपैथिक से ही नुकसान होगा
says: If the planet behind a medicine system is afflicted, that system fails: bad Mercury means Ayurveda never helps, bad Mars means allopathy does nothing and surgery is needed, bad Moon means homeopathy itself causes harm (flagged health claim).
cells_derived_method: 'खराब' (bad) is read from dignity and house: debilitation or placement in the 6th, 8th or 12th would count as bad. He does not define it, so this is my reading.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Mercury debilitated in Pisces in the 6th house, lagna Libra; Ayurveda would not help this person by his rule.
Derived: Mars debilitated in Cancer in the 8th house, lagna Sagittarius; allopathic medicine alone is not enough and surgery is the route.
Derived: Moon debilitated in Scorpio in the 3rd house, lagna Virgo; homeopathy is the system to avoid.

ambiguity: The sentence crosses the caption break at 'होमोपैथिक से ही | नुकसान होगा'; 'ही' may mean even homeopathy alone harms.
classical_check: Silent; this is his own extension of planet-to-system mapping.

hindi: यह सारे की सारी कहानिया इसके अंदर बन जाती है
says: All the stories about which therapy cured which person fit inside this planet-to-system scheme.
ambiguity: 'इसके अंदर' points back to the planet-to-medicine mapping just given.
classical_check: Silent; a claim of explanatory coverage that is not tested here.

hindi: उसके बाद आपका शनि के थ्रू ठीक होना है एक्यूपंचर प्रेशर एक्यूपंक्चर एक्यूप्रेशर यह शनि महाराज की कृपा
says: Saturn's medicine is acupuncture and acupressure: if you are to be cured through Saturn, this is Saturn's grace (flagged health claim).
ambiguity: 'एक्यूपंचर प्रेशर' is caption noise for acupuncture and acupressure.
classical_check: Silent; Saturn as karaka of pain and of bones and joints is classical, therapies are not.

hindi: जिसकी कुंडली में जो ग्रह बलवान है उस वाली चले जाओ वह ठीक कर देगा आपको
says: Go to the therapy of whichever planet is strong in your own chart; that one will cure you.
cells_derived_method: Strength is read from sign dignity and house placement; the planet that is strong picks the therapy from the mapping he just gave (Mars allopathy, Mercury Ayurveda, Moon homeopathy, Saturn acupressure).

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Saturn exalted in Libra in the 10th house, lagna Capricorn; Saturn is the strong planet, so acupuncture or acupressure suits.
Derived: Mars exalted in Capricorn in the 3rd house, lagna Scorpio; Mars is strong, so allopathy is the system to use.
Derived: Mercury debilitated in Pisces in the 7th house, lagna Virgo; Mercury is weak, so Ayurveda is not the one and another strong planet's system must be chosen.

ambiguity: 'बलवान' is not defined; whether he means shadbala, dignity or house strength is not said.
classical_check: Using the strongest planet as the source of help is a common Jyotish idea; the therapy mapping is his own.

hindi: अगर आपकी कुंडली में केतु बहुत बढ़िया है झाड़ा लगाओ
says: If Ketu is very strong in your chart, go for jhaada (a traditional healer's brushing or exorcism-type cure).
cells_derived_method: Ketu's strength is judged by house and sign; many traditions treat 3, 6, 11 and 12 as good houses for Ketu, but he gives no list, so these examples are only my illustration.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Ketu in the 12th house in Pisces, lagna Aries; Ketu is in a moksha house and in a sign he assigns to Ketu, so jhaada-type routes would suit.
Derived: Ketu in the 6th house in Gemini, lagna Capricorn; Ketu in the house of disease and enemies is traditionally fine, so jhaada could help.

ambiguity: 'बहुत बढ़िया' is not defined as above; the sentence is a lead-in to a joke about the mantra.
classical_check: Silent on jhaada; Ketu as karaka of tantra and unseen healing is a common modern reading.

gist: Jokes that you should memorise the jhaada mantra now because he can say it only once, it is complex and will not come out the second time.

hindi: अगली बार अगर आपका राहु सेट है राहु सेट है आपका यदि तो आप अपने जीवन के अंदर सब मुझे थैंक्स बोलेंगे दवा जो दारू है उससे ठीक होंगे
says: If Rahu is well set in your chart, you will be cured by medicine that is liquor-like (alcohol-based or intoxicating); he adds that you will thank him for this (flagged health claim, not advice to drink).
cells_derived_method: Rahu 'set' is read from house and sign; Rahu is traditionally comfortable in the 3rd, 6th, 10th and 11th houses. This is my reading, he gives no list.

derived_examples.reading: Derived: Rahu in the 11th house in Gemini, lagna Leo; Rahu is well placed, so intoxicant-type or alcohol-based medicines would be the Rahu route.
Derived: Rahu in the 3rd house in Virgo, lagna Cancer; Rahu is again in a comfortable house, so the same Rahu-type medicine applies.

ambiguity: 'दारू' may be literal liquor or a loose word for strong drug-like medicines; the next rows give examples that are drugs.
classical_check: Rahu as karaka of intoxicants and poison is classical; the medicine mapping is his own.

gist: Garbled rhetorical line 'बताओ यार है कोई पैर कचर पट्टी से ठीक होंगे आप बताओ बताओ बताओ': he asks the audience to tell him something about being cured by some rubbish bandage, but the point cannot be recovered.

hindi: कोरेक्स पीते लोग कफ सिरप दारू से भरा हुआ ल नशा लोगों को क्या मिलते हैं डॉक्टर मॉर्फिन का इंजेक्शन लगाता है नशा है वो सोचो उससे ठीक करेगा
says: Examples for the Rahu-type medicine: alcohol-laden cough syrup, and the morphine injection a doctor gives, are intoxicants that still heal; he offers them as proof that liquor-like medicines are real medicine (flagged health claim, not advice).
ambiguity: Rahu is not named in this sentence; the link comes from the previous sentence, where 'दवा जो दारू है' is tied to a set Rahu.
classical_check: Rahu as karaka of intoxicants and anaesthetics is classical; naming these drugs is his own illustration.

hindi: स्टेरॉइड लगाते हैं डॉक्टर साला क्या है वो सुनन कर देता है
says: Another example: doctors give steroids, which he describes as numbing the body (flagged health claim, supports the same drug-like Rahu medicine idea).
ambiguity: 'सुनन कर देता है' is garbled; read as 'makes it numb'. Steroids do not numb, so this is a loose description.
classical_check: Silent; assigning steroids to Rahu is his own.

hindi: आज वीड बिकता है मतलब मेरवाना खुला भांग खुली बिक रही है अमेरिका कनाडा खुली इन द सेंस डॉक्टरों ने अलाउ कर दिया मेडिकल पर्पस के लिए ये कमाल हो गया है ये भी दवाई है
says: Cannabis (weed or bhang) is now sold openly in America and Canada, with doctors allowing it for medical use; he counts it as one more intoxicant that is also a medicine (a factual claim about law, not advice).
ambiguity: 'मेरवाना' is marijuana. Legality differs by country and state, and 'sold openly' overstates some places.
classical_check: Silent; bhang is linked to Shiva worship, not to a planet in the classical texts.

gist: Restates that you should follow the system of whichever planet is well placed in your chart.

hindi: इसलिए अब हमें कोई कहता है गंदी बात क्या है अच्छी बात क्या है मैं कहता हूं यार समझाना बड़ा मुश्किल है तुम्हारे लिए गंदा ये है और अच्छा वो है लेकिन गंदा क्या है अच्छा क्या है
says: What is good or bad is personal to each chart: for you this is bad and that is good, but he will not give a universal definition of good and bad.
ambiguity: The sentence ends in a question he leaves open; the universal view is taken up in the next row.
classical_check: Agrees in spirit with the Jyotish rule that a planet's result depends on lordship and house for each lagna, so the same planet is good for one chart and bad for another.

hindi: यूनिवर्सलीस कहते हैं शराब ना पिए पाप है जिस व्यक्ति का शनि और राहु का कॉमिनेशन बैठता है वह दारू की बोतल ही देगा गिफ्ट तभी उसके काम बनेंगे
says: People say liquor is a sin, but a person with a Saturn and Rahu combination will give a bottle of liquor as a gift, and only then do his works get done (flagged: a gifting remedy, not advice to drink).
